What should I know before selling a house in St. Paul?

St. Paul adds a step that most Minnesota cities lack: a city-licensed evaluator must inspect most one- and two-unit homes before the listing goes live. The city calls it Truth-in-Sale of Housing, or TISH, and it applies to single-family houses, duplexes, condominiums and townhomes.

The rest of the process looks like a sale anywhere in the state. You sign a disclosure, record a deed in Ramsey County and settle taxes at closing. Your route (agent listing, owner sale or a direct cash offer) changes the timeline more than the paperwork. The sections below cover the St. Paul rules first, then the neighborhood and housing facts that shape pricing.

What does St. Paul look like by the numbers?

The Census Bureau estimates 306,684 people lived in St. Paul on July 1, 2025. That is 1.5% fewer than the 311,503 April 2020 base, so the capital city shrank slightly while Woodbury and Sherburne County grew.

  • 125,249 households averaging 2.37 people (2020 to 2024)
  • 52.9% of homes owner-occupied, so nearly half of the housing stock is rented
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $294,500
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,911
  • Median gross rent: $1,281
  • Median household income: $73,394, with 43.8% of adults 25 and older holding a bachelor's degree

Those figures explain why many St. Paul sellers hold rental or inherited property. A house that sat as a rental for years often has deferred repairs, and the TISH report will record them for buyers.

Who needs a Truth-in-Sale of Housing report, and when?

Owners of single-family homes, duplexes, condominiums and townhomes need a TISH evaluation before the home is marketed for sale. Buildings with three or more units, commercial buildings and mixed-use buildings are outside the program. A condominium with its own Ramsey County parcel number still needs a report even when the building holds a certificate of occupancy, because that certificate only covers common areas.

The report must be available to any prospective buyer within three calendar days of listing. It stays good for 365 days and covers one sale by the owner named on it. If your offer is accepted inside that year, closing can fall after the expiration date without a new report.

The evaluator is a private contractor licensed by the city, and the evaluator sets the fee. The city does not recommend anyone. Call the Department of Safety and Inspections at 651-266-8989 before you list if you are unsure whether your sale needs a report.

What does the TISH report actually require me to fix?

Very little. The report is disclosure only, and the single mandatory item in a single-family house is a working hard-wired smoke alarm. If the evaluator marks it as a hazard, the city's electrical inspector sends a letter and you must hire a licensed electrical contractor to pull a permit and install the alarm. The contractor then calls the inspector to close the permit.

Everything else on the report informs the buyer and does not force a repair. Sellers who want to avoid hazard marks can fix items first, and the city publishes a list of the ten most common deficiencies for that purpose. Failing to follow the program is a misdemeanor under Chapter 189 of the Saint Paul Legislative Code.

Which sales are exempt from TISH?

The table lists the main rules from the city's Truth-in-Sale of Housing page.

Vacant buildingsCategory 1 needs a report before sale; Categories 2 and 3 need a code compliance inspection

Aunts, uncles and cousins do not count as immediate family under the program. The same page requires a smoking policy disclosure form when you sell a unit in a condominium, townhome or similar community, a rule that took effect January 1, 2022.

How do St. Paul's rent rules affect a rental house I want to sell?

They matter to your buyer more than to you, but they affect what the property is worth. Voters approved a rent stabilization ordinance on November 2, 2021, and the City Council amended it in September 2022 and May 2025. Rent increases are capped at 3% in a 12-month period unless an exception applies.

  • Self-certification: available for increases from 3% to 8%, evaluated each year
  • Just cause vacancy: the consumer price index change plus 8%, after city review
  • Staff determination: no fixed limit when the landlord justifies the figure
  • Separate tracks exist for new construction and for low-income housing providers

A tenant-occupied house therefore comes with limits on how fast the next owner can raise the rent. Vacant houses give a buyer more room, which is one reason investors look at emptied rentals. If tenants live in the home, ask the city's Rent Stabilization team at 651-266-8553 how the rules apply to your unit.

What shapes the housing stock across St. Paul?

Water and hills explain most of the map. The city grew at the junction of the Mississippi and Minnesota Rivers, on bluffs the glaciers cut, and it covers 56.18 square miles, of which 51.98 are land. The city planning office divides the area into 17 planning districts, and each has a council that weighs in on land use.

Older neighborhoods near downtown and along the river carry homes from the steamboat and railroad eras. The 1904 storms that damaged hundreds of downtown buildings and the 1960s freeway work, which cleared the Rondo neighborhood for Interstate 94, both left marks on where houses stand today. On the south side, the former Ford assembly plant site in Highland Park is being redeveloped as Highland Bridge, planned with about 3,800 housing units.

Winters are cold and snowy, and the city expects more spring and summer rain over time, which can lead to river and flash flooding. Buyers and inspectors in St. Paul look hard at basements, roofs and drainage for that reason.

How do transit, schools and parks affect a St. Paul sale?

Getting around is easy by Twin Cities standards. Interstates 94 and 35E cross the city, along with US 52 and Minnesota 280 and 5. The METRO Green Line runs along University Avenue to Minneapolis, the A Line serves arterial streets, and Amtrak's Empire Builder stops at Union Depot.

The city runs 160 parks and 41 recreation centers, and a 2018 ranking placed its park access second nationally behind Minneapolis. Saint Paul Public Schools is the state's largest district, and families can also use charter schools, private schools and open enrollment. Macalester College, the University of St. Thomas, Hamline University and Saint Catherine University all sit within the city, which keeps demand steady for houses near campuses.

What closing steps apply to a St. Paul house sale?

Minnesota requires a written disclosure of material facts about the property before you sign a sale agreement, under Minnesota Statutes 513.55. The disclosure must be made in good faith and reflect what you know.

The deed gets recorded where the property sits, which for St. Paul is Ramsey County. Ask the Ramsey County recorder for current recording fees and ask your title company who files the paperwork. Keep your TISH report, any smoke alarm permit and repair receipts together so your closing agent can pass copies to the buyer.

A direct sale to a cash buyer changes the schedule but the city rules above still apply to the property. Ask Safety and Inspections whether a report is needed before you accept an offer.

More questions about St. Paul, MN

Do I need a TISH report to sell my St. Paul house?

Yes, if it is a single-family home, duplex, condominium or townhome and the sale is not to immediate family. Buildings with three or more units are exempt. The report must be on hand within three calendar days of listing.

How long is a TISH report valid?

It is valid for 365 consecutive days and covers one sale by the owner named on it. If a seller accepts an offer within that year, closing may fall afterward without a new report.

What is the one repair TISH can force?

A working hard-wired smoke alarm in single-family homes. If one is missing or not working, the city sends a letter and a licensed electrician must install one under a permit.

Does Ramsey County or the city record my deed?

Ramsey County records deeds for St. Paul property. The city handles the TISH report, rental rules and permits, so you deal with two offices during a sale.

Can I sell a house with tenants in St. Paul?

Yes. Existing leases continue under the rent stabilization rules, which cap increases at 3% a year unless an exception is granted. Call the city's Rent Stabilization team at 651-266-8553 for questions about your unit.

What must a Bloomington seller do before listing a house?

Before you list, show or sell a house in Bloomington, the city requires a Time-of-Sale housing inspection and a filed evaluation report. The rule covers single and two-family dwellings, condominiums, townhouses and mobile homes, and it applies to private sales as well, including a sale to a family member that is never listed. Multi-family rental buildings of four or more units are left out.

This requirement is the biggest difference between selling here and selling in most Minnesota suburbs, so it shapes the whole timeline. Cash buyers purchase as-is, but the city's inspection step still applies to the sale. The rest of this page walks through what the inspection costs, what it can force you to fix and who can take on a hazard.

How does the Bloomington Time-of-Sale inspection work?

The owner or listing agent schedules the inspection with the city's Building and Inspections Division at 952-563-8930 or through an online request form, and the evaluator needs about 120 minutes on site. The fee is $250, which includes the energy disclosure and any re-inspections, plus a service fee of $1.95 for an e-check or 2.95 percent for a card. If you cancel before a site visit, the city offers a refund of up to 50 percent within 60 days of your request.

  • The evaluator examines visible structure, heating, electrical and plumbing, and accessible attics and crawl spaces, and does not take anything apart.
  • The report does not cover lead paint, radon or asbestos, and it does not guarantee the home.
  • The report must be displayed at the house and given to the buyer before or at sale, and a copy must reach the city within 7 calendar days.
  • The report and the Certificate of Compliance are good for one year and only for the owner named on them.

Since April 2022 the inspection has included an energy disclosure covering the heating and cooling system, water heater, insulation and windows, and the city says no energy upgrades are required of the seller.

What counts as an immediate hazard, and who pays to fix it?

Only nine categories of defect must be corrected, and the seller is responsible unless the buyer agrees in writing to take them over. The city lists them as unsafe heating systems, unsafe water heaters, dangerous electrical conditions, unsanitary plumbing, structures unable to carry their loads, roofs, walls and foundations that are not weather tight, abandoned fuel tanks, unsanitary refuse or infestation, and missing or non-working smoke detectors.

Other defects are noted in the report but do not have to be repaired. If hazards are found, a re-inspection by a city inspector is required before the house can be occupied, and the owner or contractor must pull any permits. A buyer who is willing to take the hazards must get the city's written consent by signing a Hazard Correction/Responsibility form, which is currently handled through DocuSign by calling the same 952-563-8930 line. The Certificate of Compliance is typically required at closing.

Which sales are exempt from the Bloomington inspection?

Five kinds of transfer are exempt, but you must still call the city to say which exemption you are using. They are a newly built dwelling transferred to its first owner, a multiple dwelling already licensed as rental, a sale to a public body, a sale for demolition, and a sale by a sheriff or other court officer. The last exemption does not cover a sale by someone appointed by a probate court, which matters for heirs selling an inherited Bloomington house.

If your sale does not fit an exemption, plan for the inspection and the report date before you set a closing. Check any open work permits as well, because the owner or contractor must obtain the necessary permits and the dwelling is subject to re-inspection of open permits before occupancy.

Bloomington is a mid-priced suburb in which 65.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the median home value is $361,700. The table compares the figures a seller uses to sense-check a price.

Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts for Bloomington. The same-house rate is 87.5 percent, and 19.8 percent speak a language other than English at home.

What is Bloomington like, and who shops for homes here?

Bloomington is the largest suburb in the Twin Cities, with 89,034 people, 10 miles south of downtown Minneapolis on the north bank of the Minnesota River. It was settled in 1843, the Town of Bloomington was incorporated on May 11, 1858, and it became a city on November 8, 1960. The postwar housing boom filled in much of the street grid you see today.

Interstate 35W divides the city informally. West Bloomington is mostly residential with newer housing, while East Bloomington has more industry, retail and the less expensive housing. Highway 77 (Cedar Avenue), Highway 169 and Interstate 494 frame the rest of the map, and the Metro Blue Line light rail runs from the Mall of America to downtown Minneapolis and both airport terminals.

The employer base is strong. Mall of America tenants are the largest group, with Dayforce, Donaldson, Great Clips, HealthPartners and Toro headquartered here. ISD 271 runs fifteen public schools, with John F. Kennedy High School in the east and Thomas Jefferson High School in the west, and the attendance line runs near France and Xerxes Avenues. A buyer will ask which side of that line you are on.

Which city fees and bills should a seller check before closing?

Before closing, call the city to find out whether anything is owed on the property, because outstanding items are easier to clear before the title company asks. The city's Time-of-Sale page lists the right numbers.

  • Assessing Division: 952-563-8722, for fees or fines associated with the property.
  • Utility Billing: 952-563-8726, for the current outstanding water bill.
  • Environmental Health: 952-563-8934, for pending civil fines.
  • Finance: 952-563-4527, for pending weeds, trees, brush removal and abatements.

Hennepin County bills the property tax, due May 15 and October 15, and it takes recordings by appointment, online through its Virtual Recorder site with a $3 service fee, by mail or through eRecording for title companies. Its recording page lists a $46 fee per document and a $54 well disclosure certificate when one is needed, and it says properties with delinquent taxes cannot be transferred under Minnesota Statute 272.12. Minnesota Statute 513.55 separately requires a written seller disclosure before the purchase agreement is signed.

More questions about Bloomington, MN

Is the Bloomington inspection required for a cash sale?

Yes, it applies to any sale of a covered dwelling, cash or financed, listed or private. The only way out is one of the five exemptions in city code, and you still have to call the city to say which one applies.

Do I have to repair everything the Bloomington inspector finds?

No. Only the nine immediate hazard categories must be corrected, and the buyer can assume them with the city's written consent. Other deficiencies are listed in the report without a repair requirement.

How long is a Bloomington Time-of-Sale report valid?

One year from the date of issue, and only for the owner named on it.

Who gets the Certificate of Compliance?

The city sends it to the owner or listing agent once no hazards remain. It is typically required at closing, so ask your agent or title company to confirm they have it before the signing date.

Can an heir selling an inherited house in Bloomington skip the inspection?

Usually not. The sheriff and court-officer exemption does not apply to a sale by a person appointed by a probate court, so a personal representative should plan for the inspection and report.

What should I expect when selling a house in Woodbury?

Woodbury is one of the pricier east metro suburbs, and most sales here involve newer houses, active buyers and a short list of city rules about rentals and permits. The city is eight miles east of St. Paul along Interstate 94 in Washington County, and it is the seventh most populous city in Minnesota.

Because the houses are comparatively young, repair problems tend to be smaller than in older cities. The sellers who struggle are usually the ones with a tenant in place, an inherited house far from family, or a deadline that rules out a showing schedule.

What do the Census figures show for Woodbury?

Woodbury had an estimated 81,558 residents on July 1, 2025, a gain of 8.6% over the April 2020 base of 75,105. It counted 61,961 people in 2010 and 46,463 in 2000, so the city has grown by about 75% since 2000.

  • 29,312 households averaging 2.66 people (2020 to 2024)
  • 77.6% of homes owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $450,200
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,412
  • Median gross rent: $1,908
  • Median household income: $125,310
  • 61.3% of adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree, and 5.3% of residents in poverty

Families dominate: 25.8% of residents are under 18, and the 2020 census found children in 38.2% of households and married couples in 59.9%. South Washington County Schools, District 833, is the city's second largest employer after M Health Fairview, which shows how closely local life is tied to the school system.

High values mean a seller's equity is usually large, so the main question is speed and certainty rather than whether the sale clears the loan.

How did Woodbury grow from farmland to a suburb?

The area was first settled in 1844 and was originally called Red Rock before the name changed to honor Levi Woodbury, because another Red Rock Township already existed in Minnesota. It was mostly woods at first and then became farmland, and the township government was organized in 1858.

The first suburban development, Woodbury Heights, broke ground in 1955. Voters turned down a joint incorporation with Cottage Grove in 1963, 1,284 to 662, and then approved incorporating Woodbury alone on February 14, 1967, by 543 to 164. The village was officially incorporated on March 7, 1967. A 2025 estimate of 81,558 shows how far that decision carried it.

What does the land and neighborhood layout look like?

Woodbury covers 35.722 square miles, of which 34.895 are land. Interstate 94 forms the northern edge, 60th Street South the southern, Century Avenue the west and Manning Avenue the east. Neighbors include Oakdale, Lake Elmo, Cottage Grove, Maplewood, Newport and Afton.

The city sits on upland between the Mississippi and St. Croix river valleys. Small lakes dot it, including Powers, Wilmes, Colby and Carver, and the northeast corner drains to Valley Creek, one of the few remaining trout streams in the Twin Cities area. Woodbury maintains 63 parks covering about 3,600 acres and around 180 miles of mostly paved trails, which tends to be a selling point for houses near the lakes.

Climate data for the city show a January mean daily high of 23 degrees and a July high of 83, with about 32.6 inches of precipitation a year. Roofs, gutters and furnaces get tested every season.

What must a Woodbury landlord do before selling a rental house?

Any single family home, townhome or condominium rented in Woodbury needs a city rental license, and the license expires December 31 each year. There is no exemption for owners with only one rental unit. Exceptions exist for family-occupied homes, state-licensed nursing homes, some contract-for-deed sales while the buyer lives there, a fee waiver for owners on active military duty, and small state-licensed residential settings.

Woodbury single-dwelling rental license facts from the City of Woodbury rental licensing pages

Contact651-414-3414 or rental@woodburymn.gov

Applications for 2027 are not open yet and will be available after the City Council adopts the 2027 fee schedule. Mid-year additions are pro-rated by quarter. A buyer who plans to keep a tenant should ask the Code Enforcement Division how the license transfers.

Are short-term rentals allowed in Woodbury?

No. City code prohibits renting a property for a term shorter than 30 days when the renter's permanent residence is elsewhere. That matters for a buyer who is pricing a house on vacation-rental income, and for a seller whose listing history shows nightly bookings.

Tell any serious buyer about past short-term use up front. The disclosure rules ask sellers to share material facts they know, and a code violation fits that description.

Which permits come up when you fix a Woodbury house for sale?

Woodbury uses a combination permit system. One permit covers building, plumbing, heating and cooling, and electrical fees for additions, basement finishes, decks, porches, remodels, repairs and new construction. Stand-alone flat-fee permits cover single replacements such as a furnace, air conditioner, water heater, water softener or EV charger outlet, and they go to the licensed contractor doing the work or to the homeowner.

  • Applications go through the city's online permitting portal
  • Residential contractors must hold a valid Minnesota license or a mechanical bond
  • Morning inspection windows run 9:30 to 11:30 a.m., so call by 9 a.m.
  • Afternoon windows run 1:30 to 3:30 p.m., so call by 1 p.m.

Call the Building Inspections Division at 651-714-3543 if you are unsure whether a project needs a permit. Finish and close any open permits before listing so a buyer's lender does not find them.

What taxes and recording steps apply at a Woodbury closing?

The deed is recorded with the Washington County Recorder. Whichever route you choose, the same Minnesota paperwork applies, and the county that records your deed is almost always Anoka County.

Where is Blaine, and who buys homes there?

Blaine is a fast-growing suburb that sits mostly in Anoka County, with a piece in Ramsey County, and its buyers are mainly commuters and families. The city's own history says the population passed 75,000 by 2025, making Blaine the largest city in Anoka County. The count was 1,694 in 1950 and reached 70,222 at the 2020 count.

The land explains the housing. Sandy soil and wetlands discouraged farming, so dairy and sod farms later gave way to subdivisions. Developers in areas such as The Lakes and Club West dredged ponds and used the sand to raise the building sites, and Sunrise Lake in The Lakes is the largest water body in the city at 158 acres. Laddie Lake, at 77 acres, is the only natural lake.

Main routes are Interstate 35W, Highway 65, Highway 10, Highway 610, University Avenue, Lexington Avenue and Hamline Avenue. The National Sports Center opened in 1990 and the TPC Twin Cities golf course in 2000, and the sports center has more than 50 full-size soccer fields plus an eight-sheet ice arena.

Three districts serve Blaine, and the one tied to your address is a real selling point. Anoka-Hennepin covers most of the city, including the area from Highway 65 to University Avenue north of 99th Avenue NE. Spring Lake Park Schools covers nearly everything south of 99th Avenue NE, and Centennial Schools covers the area east of Lexington Avenue and south and east of Interstate 35W.

The city has Blaine High School in Anoka-Hennepin, Centennial High School, and Paladin Career and Technical High School, a public charter school. Anoka County records the deed, and its rules decide whether the document is accepted. Its recording requirements page lists what a transfer deed must carry.

Residential homestead property in Anoka County is billed in two halves, due the middle of May and of October (the 15th of each), and the county notes that late payment brings penalties even if you never received a statement. The county's page also says a Certificate of Real Estate Value is due at the auditor's office when a property sells, as Minnesota Statute 272.115 requires. A qualifying disabled veteran can receive a market value exclusion of up to $300,000 on homestead property, so buyers who are veterans may ask about it. Have the closing agent split the current half-year between you and the buyer by closing date.

What disclosures does a Blaine seller owe?

Before you sign a purchase agreement for a residential property, Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires written disclosure of material facts you know that could adversely and significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment. Section 144.496 adds a radon disclosure: whether tests were done, the latest reports, any mitigation system, a radon warning statement and the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

The city sits on glacial sand, ponds and wetlands, so basement moisture is a fair thing to document. Gather any sump pump records, past repairs and test results before the first showing so the written disclosure is accurate and complete.

Minnesota's state deed tax is imposed on the deed and is calculated at .0033 of the net consideration above $3,000. Ask your title company who pays it under your purchase agreement, since the agreement decides that.

Is a rental license transferable to the buyer of my Blaine rental?

Check with Blaine Housing Services before closing. The license is issued yearly and expires on December 31, so the new owner should expect to apply for their own and schedule any inspection the city requires.

What if my Blaine house has radon or basement water problems?

Disclose what you know in writing. Minnesota law requires disclosure of known radon test results and of material facts that could significantly affect a buyer, and a seller who skips them can be held liable for damages.

It depends on the buyer and the title work, but a cash sale has no lender appraisal, so closing is often a matter of weeks. Anoka County's recording checklist is the main step that can delay a closing if something is missing.

What should a seller know about the city of St. Cloud?

St. Cloud serves as seat of Stearns County, and the city also reaches into Benton and Sherburne counties. It lies on both banks of the Mississippi River, with the Sauk River along its northern edge, about 65 miles northwest of the Twin Cities. Interstate 94, U.S. Highways 10 and 52, and State Highways 15 and 23 serve it (Wikipedia).

Settlers founded three separate villages starting in 1853, called Upper Town, Middle Town and Lower Town, and the city incorporated in 1856. Ravines that once divided them are still visible. Granite quarries opened in the 1880s and gave the city the nickname Granite City.

  • Schools: most of the city is in the St. Cloud Area School District, and part of the Benton County portion is in Sauk Rapids-Rice Public Schools.

Buyers of a St. Cloud house often ask how it has been used, whether as an owner's home, a licensed rental or a vacant property, so the paper trail matters.

The city runs complaint response and routine rental inspections through its Housing and Code Enforcement division, and it publishes information sheets on accessory structures, fences, off-street parking and recreational vehicles. Check those items on your own lot, because a shed, fence or parked trailer that does not meet the rules is easy to fix before an inspection.

The city also publishes a flyer on bed bugs for owners. Rental training questions go to the Police Department's information desk at 320-345-4444. If a rental has had a past infestation, have the treatment records ready to show a buyer.

Can I sell a St. Cloud rental house with tenants in it?

Do I need rental training to hold a St. Cloud rental license?

Is St. Cloud mostly renters or owners?

What is different about selling a house in St. Louis Park?

St. Louis Park requires a city housing inspection whenever a property is sold or ownership is transferred. That step comes before closing, so it shapes how fast any sale can go, whether you list the house or take a cash offer.

The city is a first-ring suburb immediately west of Minneapolis, bordered by Edina, Golden Valley, Minnetonka, Plymouth and Hopkins. The Census Bureau estimates 50,027 residents for July 2025, nearly the same as the 50,010 counted in the 2020 census. Interstate 394, U.S. Highway 169 and State Highways 7 and 100 run through it, and the public schools belong to Independent School District 283.

  • Listing: the inspection is arranged by the seller, and corrections are usually made before the closing.
  • Direct sale: the same inspection applies, so book it early.
  • Cash offer: a buyer can take the house with open corrections through the city's escrow option, described below.

How does the St. Louis Park sale inspection work?

A city inspector visits for about 45 to 60 minutes to check that the siding, roof, garage and interior meet the city's property maintenance code. Appointments are usually available within one to three days.

The fee covers the first inspection and any follow-ups: $360 for a single-family house or townhouse, $460 for a duplex and $250 for a condominium. With no violations, the city issues a property maintenance certificate. It lasts one year for a house, townhouse or duplex and two years for a condo (City of St. Louis Park).

If violations turn up, the city issues a correction notice. In most cases repairs must meet the code in force when the building was built, and remodeled areas follow the code from the year of the remodel. Smoke detectors are the exception and are required in every building.

  • Seller repairs: the usual path, followed by a return visit to verify the work.
  • Temporary certificate: a buyer may take a temporary property maintenance certificate by signing an escrow agreement and finishing the work within 90 days of closing.
  • Cost and timing: the escrow agreement costs $155, must be prepared 48 hours before closing, and needs enough money held in escrow to cover the listed work.

What happened to St. Louis Park's housing stock?

Most houses here date from one building boom. St. Louis Park grew from 7,737 people in 1940 to 22,644 in 1950 and 43,310 in 1960, and about 60 percent of its homes went up between the late 1940s and early 1950s. Between 1950 and 1956 alone, 66 new subdivisions were recorded for 2,700 homes (Wikipedia).

The settlement was named for the Minneapolis and St. Louis Railway, with Park added to avoid confusion with St. Louis, Missouri. It incorporated as a village in 1886, and voters adopted a home rule charter in 1954 that made it a city with a hired manager. The Peavey-Haglin elevator from 1899 still stands as the world's first concrete tubular grain elevator.

That history matters to a seller because the inspector reads each house against the code in place when it was built. Roofs, siding, garages and interiors are the four areas the city names, so walk those first.

  • Before the visit: the city publishes a list of commonly noted property maintenance deficiencies as a PDF.
  • Permits: all open permits must be closed before an escrow agreement can be approved.
  • Questions: the city's escrow line is 952.924.2588.

Do St. Louis Park rental rules affect a sale?

Yes. The city requires an annual business license before a tenant moves into a single-family home, duplex, townhome or condo that the owner does not occupy. Rental licenses cover non-owner-occupied units, including one and two single-family homes, townhomes, condominiums and multifamily buildings.

The license requirement does not apply to a dwelling the owner occupies for at least six months per calendar year, or to rooms rented inside an owner-occupied home. A seller renting a house should confirm the license is current, since a buyer who keeps the tenant will inherit that duty. The city also offers rental license ordinance training for owners (City of St. Louis Park).

If you are selling a house you have rented, a sale inspection still applies at transfer. Ask the city's Housing office whether anything else is due at transfer before you set a closing date.

How do Hennepin County taxes work for a St. Louis Park seller?

Hennepin County bills property tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, or the next business day when either falls on a weekend or holiday. Late payments carry penalties that grow each month, and a late payment is applied to penalty first and then to tax.

St. Louis Park runs its own assessing office, so valuation notices come from the city rather than the county. You can reach it at 952-924-2535. Notices go out in March, informal discussion happens in April and May, and the county board of appeal and equalization meets in mid-June (Hennepin County Assessment).

Payment is flexible. Hennepin accepts e-checks online with no fee, up to $50,000 per transaction, and card, PayPal or Venmo payments with a service fee. Many owners instead pay through a mortgage escrow account, in which case the lender receives the payment information, so ask the servicer for the payoff before closing.

  • Penalty abatement: an owner may ask once every ten years, with applications due June 30 for the first half and November 30 for the second.
  • Delinquency: taxes unpaid by January 1 of the next year become delinquent, with a one-year or three-year redemption period by property class.
  • Questions: Hennepin property tax staff are at 612-348-3011 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and they reply to email within about one business day.

How long is the St. Louis Park property maintenance certificate good for?

It lasts one year for single-family homes, townhomes and duplexes, and two years for condominiums. It is issued once an inspector finds no code violations or confirms repairs are complete.

Can the buyer finish the repairs after closing in St. Louis Park?

Yes, through a temporary property maintenance certificate. The buyer signs an escrow agreement, funds the cost of the work, pays a $155 fee, and completes everything within 90 days of closing. Call 952.924.2588 with questions.

When are Hennepin County property taxes due for a St. Louis Park house?

They are due May 15 and October 15. When either date falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

Who assesses property in St. Louis Park?

The city's own assessing office handles valuation notices, and its number is 952-924-2535. Hennepin County handles tax billing and collection, so keep both offices in your contact list. Hennepin's assessment page lists the same number for St. Louis Park assessing questions, including requests for an open book discussion.

How can you sell a house fast in Shakopee, Minnesota?

Three routes exist here: hire an agent, handle a private sale, or take cash from a buyer who skips the lender. Speed depends on the house, the title, and how quickly the Scott County paperwork can be gathered.

The Census Bureau counted 43,698 people in Shakopee in April 2020 and estimates 49,366 for July 2025, a gain of about 5,700 people in five years. A house that needs a new roof, a tenant move-out, or an estate clean-out still sells here, but each of those problems changes which route makes sense.

  • Selling it yourself: saves the agent fee but leaves pricing, disclosures and the purchase agreement to you.

What should a seller know about Shakopee itself?

Shakopee serves as seat of Scott County, set on the south bank bend of the Minnesota River southwest of Minneapolis. Thomas Holmes platted Shakopee Village in 1854 and named it after Chief Shakopee II. The city first incorporated in 1857, gave up its charter in 1861, and incorporated again in 1870 (Wikipedia).

For most of the twentieth century it was a small river town. Growth took off after U.S. Highway 169 was realigned in 1996 toward the Bloomington Ferry Bridge, and the population went from 20,568 in 2000 to 37,076 in 2010. County Highway 101 runs east and west through the historic downtown, while Highway 169 and State Highway 13 tie the city to the rest of the metro.

  • Landmarks buyers recognise: Valleyfair, Canterbury Park, and the Landing, a historic village on the river.
  • Public schools: Shakopee Public Schools, Independent School District 720, with Shakopee High School and two middle schools.
  • Land area: 28.44 square miles in the 2020 Census, with U.S. Highway 169 and State Highway 13 as the main links to Minneapolis and Saint Paul.

Do Shakopee rules affect a rental house you want to sell?

Yes. The city requires every rental property, including a single-family home, to be registered, and the registration runs through the Shakopee ePortal. A house with a tenant in it carries that history into the sale.

The city's R-HOME program asks owners to finish Phase I landlord training within a year of receiving a rental certificate, and properties with four or more units must complete Phases I, II and III. Background checks on prospective tenants must be done before a tenant occupies the unit. A buyer who plans to keep the tenant will ask whether the certificate and training are current.

  • Registration: file it online through the city ePortal.
  • Training: the Phase I certificate is accepted by other cities, and the city usually hosts a session in spring.
  • Fair housing: the City Council approved a Fair Housing Policy in May 2019, and complaints go to the Minnesota Department of Human Rights, since the city does not take them in.

Questions about fair housing duties during a sale can go to the city's Department of Planning and Development at 952-233-9300. For a rented house, ask the buyer early whether they want the tenant to stay, because that decides whether you need a move-out date written into the contract.

How does Scott County value and tax a Shakopee house?

Scott County's assessor sets the value, and the tax bill follows from it. State law makes the assessor physically review 20 percent of all property each year, so your neighborhood is visited about once every five years. Value notices are mailed in or around March.

You may decline an interior inspection. The assessor then estimates the interior, and the local board of review cannot lower your value until you allow the inspection. Value can rise or fall by any amount, since the old 15 percent limit program ended with taxes payable in 2010 (Scott County Property and Taxation Services).

  • First half: due May 15, with payment by mail, drop box, online, or at the Government Center at 200 4th Avenue West in Shakopee.
  • Second half: due October 15.
  • Homestead and veteran relief: Scott County takes residential homestead applications and helps eligible honorably discharged veterans with service-connected disabilities claim the state's market value exclusion, so check whether a relief program is attached to the parcel you are selling.
  • Appeals: the county says you have until April 30 of the year the taxes are due to file with the Minnesota Tax Court.
  • Mailing: the Postal Service now postmarks the date mail is first processed, so the county suggests asking for a manual postmark or paying online.

What should you check before closing a Shakopee sale?

Start with the county's property information site, which shows the legal description, tax detail, valuation, recorded documents and the certificate of real estate value for a parcel. Searching by address works best with the house number and the first few letters of the street name.

The information refreshes weekly, so call Property and Taxation Services at 952-496-8115 for a current payoff figure, especially if the parcel is under a confession of judgment contract for past-due years.

  • Confirm the owner on record matches the person signing the deed.
  • Ask the county for the balance of both halves, including any special assessments.
  • If the house was a rental, gather the registration and training certificate.
  • If an heir is selling, ask the county recorder what must be on file before the deed can be recorded.

A closing agent normally orders these searches, but a seller who has them ready avoids delay. If the sale is a quick cash purchase, the same items let the buyer's title company move straight to a closing date.

Is a cash offer faster than listing a house in Shakopee?

It can be, because there is no buyer loan or lender appraisal to wait on. Closing time still depends on title work, so a clean title closes sooner than one with liens or an open estate.

Do I have to let the Scott County assessor inside my house?

No. You can decline an interior inspection, and the assessor will estimate the interior. The catch is that the local board of review cannot change your value in your favor until you allow the inspection.

When are Shakopee property taxes due?

The first half is due May 15 and the second half October 15. Scott County also notes that mail postmarks now show the day USPS first processes the item, so pay online or request a manual postmark near a deadline.

Does Shakopee require rental registration when I sell a rented house?

Rental registration is required for any rental in the city, single-family homes included, and it is filed through the ePortal. Owners also complete R-HOME Phase I training within a year of receiving a certificate, so have those records ready for a buyer.

Where do I find out what I still owe on a Shakopee parcel?

Use the Scott County property information search, then call Property and Taxation Services at 952-496-8115 for a current figure. The online data updates weekly, so a phone check before closing is worth the few minutes.

What should a seller know about Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota?

Inver Grove Heights is a Dakota County city of 36,873 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, with a land area of about 27.9 square miles. It lies roughly nine miles southeast of Saint Paul, and Newport and Saint Paul Park sit across the Mississippi River from it.

Irish and German farmers claimed land here after the 1851 Treaty of Traverse des Sioux, and the township took its name from the Irish village of Inver and the German town of Grove. By 1880 there were 240 farms, four churches and four school districts. The village of Inver Grove and Inver Grove Township merged to form the city on March 9, 1965, and the population climbed from 6,266 in 1960 to 29,751 in 2000.

Notable local landmarks include District 7 School, Dakota County's first public school (1854), the 1894 Rock Island Swing Bridge, now a park, and the site where a B-52 bomber crashed on September 16, 1958. Southern Inver Grove Heights also holds the Pine Bend Bluffs Scientific and Natural Area, where a roughly 500 million year old impact crater was identified in 2022.

What do Census figures say about Inver Grove Heights homes?

The city has an older population and a mix of owners and renters. About 76.9 percent of units are owner-occupied and the median home value is $363,400 for 2020-2024, while 17.9 percent of residents are 65 or older. Older owners downsizing or heirs handling an estate are common sellers here.

What are the ways to sell an Inver Grove Heights house quickly?

Most owners choose among a traditional listing, a sale without an agent, or an as-is cash purchase. The right choice depends on the house and your timeline.

  • A listing works well for an updated house in a school area buyers ask for, such as Simley High School's attendance area, but it adds showings, inspection requests and loan approval time.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale keeps the commission with you, though you handle disclosures, the purchase agreement and negotiation yourself.
  • A cash buyer purchases without repairs or cleaning, which suits estate houses, tenant-occupied properties and homes with deferred maintenance.

With a median home value of $363,400 and 17.9 percent of residents over 65, estate and downsizing sales are a regular part of the local market. Whichever path you take, line up the final water read, the deed tax and any county clearance steps early so the closing date holds.

Can I rent out or list an Inver Grove Heights house on Airbnb?

Not for stays shorter than 30 days unless the home is owner-occupied. Inver Grove Heights changed its short-term rental rules effective April 1, 2025, so properties that are not the owner's residence may only be rented for 30 days or more, including those listed on Airbnb or Vrbo.

Long-term rentals need a city rental license. In October 2025 the city sent license holders a letter about proposed amendments: a one-year license term, a January 31 renewal deadline with an April 1 through March 31 license period, a property manager living within 75 miles, and a three-tier fine structure. The final vote was expected after a November 10, 2025 reading. Ask the city clerk for the terms in force today if you are selling a house that is currently rented.

Buyers who plan to keep the house as a rental will want the license history, so gather it before you list.

Which Inver Grove Heights code rules can slow a sale?

The city's code enforcement office publishes the rules most often cited on residential lots, and a pre-listing walk-around helps.

  • Grass must stay under eight inches, and brush piles are not allowed.
  • Fences need a permit before installation, with a 48 inch limit in the front yard and seven feet in side and back yards.
  • Vehicles stored outside need current tabs and must run. Inoperable vehicles belong in a garage.
  • Roll-off dumpsters cannot sit in the street and may stay on a lot only three months out of twelve unless an extension is granted.
  • Parking on any city street is banned from 3:00 to 6:00 AM between November 1 and April 1.

Home businesses must be run entirely inside the dwelling with no visible signs, which matters if you are selling a house that doubles as a workshop. Violations are reported through the city's RequestTracker, and the Code Compliance Division answers questions at 651-450-2491.

Which schools and employers shape the Inver Grove Heights market?

Most of the city belongs to Inver Grove Heights Community Schools, Independent School District 199. It runs Simley High School, Inver Grove Heights Middle School, and Hilltop, Pine Bend and Salem Hills elementary schools. The western part of the city is in District 196 (Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan), and a small northwest piece is in District 197. Inver Hills Community College is also inside the city.

CHS, Inc. keeps its headquarters here, and the city's 2021 financial report listed Cenex and CHS Cooperatives as the largest employer with about 1,600 workers. The Pine Bend Refinery, the largest in Minnesota, straddles the border with Rosemount, and Gertens Greenhouses is a major garden center. The main roads are I-494, US 52, and Minnesota Highways 55 and 3.

How do I handle city water, deeds and disclosures when selling in Inver Grove Heights?

For water and sewer, call Utility Billing at 651-450-2520 well ahead of your move; the city asks newcomers for at least one week of notice to arrange a meter reading, and sellers should set the final read the same way.

Dakota County Property Taxation and Records records the deed. State deed tax at 0.0033 of the net price comes to about $1,199 on the city's $363,400 median home value. Dakota County's selling-property page flags extra steps for manufactured homes, for properties with wells or septic systems, and for owners on Medical Assistance, who may need a certificate of clearance from the county at 651-554-6555.

If sewage on the property does not go to a permitted facility, state law requires a written septic disclosure before the purchase agreement is signed, and a seller who knew of the system and failed to disclose it can owe the buyer the cost of bringing it into compliance (Minnesota Statutes 115.55, subdivision 6). Dakota County's 2026 open book appeal period ran March 11 to May 1 and the board of appeal met June 8, so any value challenge for this year has closed.

Can I sell an Inver Grove Heights house that has tenants?

Yes. Give the buyer the lease and the city rental license details. Because the city has been revising its rental licensing ordinance, ask the City Clerk what the license term and renewal rules are before you list.

How much notice does Inver Grove Heights utility billing need?

The city asks for at least one week of notice to schedule a water meter reading, and its number is 651-450-2520. Contact them before closing so the seller's final bill is accurate.

What is deed tax on an Inver Grove Heights sale?

State deed tax is 0.0033 of the net consideration when it is above $3,000. At the Census median home value of $363,400 that is about $1,199. Dakota County collects it when the deed is recorded.

Do I need a septic disclosure when selling in Inver Grove Heights?

Only if sewage on the property does not go to a permitted facility. Under Minnesota Statutes 115.55, you must then describe the system and map it before the purchase agreement is signed. If the house is on city sewer, the disclosure is a simple statement to that effect.

Are there special steps if the owner is on Medical Assistance?

Dakota County says residents on Medical Assistance have requirements when selling, and it runs a certificates of clearance office at 651-554-6555. Call before you accept an offer so the paperwork does not delay closing.

How do you sell a house quickly in Brooklyn Center, MN?

The quickest sales in Brooklyn Center are those where the owner knows the city's rental, vacancy and utility rules before an offer arrives. Brooklyn Center is a first-ring suburb in Hennepin County with 31,846 residents, and most of its land is single-family homes. Rental licensing and vacant building registration are the two city programs a seller is most likely to meet.

  • An owner-occupied house with no code orders can be listed or sold directly with little city involvement.
  • A rental needs a current city license and a record of its inspection.
  • A vacant house may need to be registered with the city and re-inspected before anyone moves in.

Work out which of the three describes your property, then read the matching section below.

What is Brooklyn Center, and what shapes its housing?

Brooklyn Center sits on the Mississippi River just north of Minneapolis and covers 8.4 square miles, of which 8.0 is land. The area was settled in 1852, formed a village from parts of Brooklyn Township and Crystal Lake Township on February 18, 1911, and became a charter city on December 8, 1966. Farmland was sold to builders in the 1940s, and the population reached 4,000 by 1950. Dayton's opened the Brookdale shopping center in 1960, when the city had passed 24,000 people.

The river is the eastern boundary. Upper Twin Lake (117 acres) feeds a chain of lakes that drain to Shingle Creek, the city has 26 parks and 20 miles of trails, and Palmer Lake Park preserves more than 200 acres of lake and marsh. The Heritage Center, the former Cap Martin estate that later passed to Earle Brown, is now a city-owned conference and event site. The main street, Brooklyn Boulevard, replaced the old Osseo Road route. Public schools are in Brooklyn Center Schools, ISD 286.

The city sits in plant hardiness zone 4b, where winter lows can reach minus 25 degrees, so heating, insulation and roof condition are worth documenting for a buyer.

Do you need a rental license to sell a Brooklyn Center rental?

You need one to operate the rental, and the buyer of a rental will ask to see it. Brooklyn Center has licensed rental property since June 1, 1975, and the rule covers any housing that is not owner-occupied, whatever the tax status or whether rent is charged. Short-term rentals such as Airbnb need a rental license too, but an owner-occupied house renting one or more rooms and approved accessory dwelling units do not.

In May 2026 the city adopted a two-year rental license. Every license is now issued for two years and must pass an inspection that uses city codes, the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code and applicable Minnesota codes. Operating without a license is a misdemeanor and can bring administrative citations and fines. If you are selling a licensed rental, give the buyer the license, the inspection results and the lease files and ask the city whether the buyer must apply for a new license.

What if the house is vacant when you sell?

Brooklyn Center requires a vacant building registration, and the fees climb the longer the house sits empty. Residential fees listed on the city's application, revised June 27, 2025, are shown below.

  • Single-family or townhome, vacant up to one year: $595 total ($195 re-occupancy inspection plus $400 registration).
  • Condo, up to one year: $515.
  • Duplex, triplex or fourplex under one owner: $675, $815 or $950.
  • Any residential type vacant one to three years: $1,000 a year.
  • Vacant more than three years: $3,000 a year.

The registration fee can be reduced by up to $300 if the property has no code violations, but you must call 763-569-3330 and meet the inspector on site before applying. The form says the first year of vacancy needs both the registration and a re-occupancy inspection, that sellers must tell buyers about correction orders, and that the buyer can take over responsibility for corrections by contacting the city. The ordinance's purpose is to protect neighborhoods from hazards and blight, and failing to comply is a misdemeanor.

How do utilities and special assessments work at sale?

Brooklyn Center bills water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, street lights and recycling quarterly, and it generates a final bill when a property is sold. The city says final bills are produced several times a month. Delinquent utility bills are certified to property taxes each year as special assessments, with a $50 certification fee added, so a balance you ignore can follow the parcel onto the buyer's tax bill. The minimum residential bill for 2026 is $227.17 a quarter, or $174.43 with the senior sewer rate.

Special assessments for city projects are paid through the Community Development Department at 763-569-3330 before they roll over to county taxes. Ask that office for a payoff figure, and confirm it with your title company before the closing date.

Who handles assessing, taxes and recording for Brooklyn Center?

Hennepin County does all three, not the city. The county assesses the roughly 8,986 parcels in Brooklyn Center, sets estimated market value and classification, reviews each property in person every five years, and takes homestead applications at its assessor's office at 612-348-3046. A new owner has to file for homestead to receive the reduced taxable value, and the application asks for Social Security numbers of owners who live there and the Certificate of Real Estate Value.

Property tax is due May 15 and October 15, and Hennepin accepts payment online, by mail, at the Government Center or by direct payment. Taxes can be included in a mortgage payment through escrow. For recording, Hennepin County Recorder fees are $46 per document, a well disclosure certificate is $54, and an eCRV is required for deeds with taxable consideration over $3,000. Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires you to give a buyer written disclosure of material facts before the agreement is signed.

More questions about Brooklyn Center, MN

Does Brooklyn Center require an inspection when I sell my home?

Inspections apply to licensed rentals and to vacant buildings, which need a re-occupancy inspection. For an owner-occupied house, call Community Development at 763-569-3330 to confirm whether anything applies to your address.

What does a vacant house cost to register in Brooklyn Center?

A single-family house vacant up to a year costs $595 in total. The fee rises to $1,000 for one to three years and $3,000 beyond three years, and up to $300 can come off the registration with a clean inspection.

Can a buyer take over code violations on a Brooklyn Center house?

Yes, the city's form says buyers can assume responsibility for corrections by contacting the city, and the sellers must tell buyers about correction orders. A buyer must also meet all city codes and the conditions of the approved property plan.

Is an Airbnb in Brooklyn Center covered by the rental license rule?

Yes. The city's rental page says short-term rental properties are required to hold a rental license. Renting out a room in an owner-occupied home is the exception.

Who do I call about homestead after I sell?

The Hennepin County Assessor's office at 612-348-3046 processes homestead for Brooklyn Center. The new owner files a homestead application with the Certificate of Real Estate Value, so give them the sale documents promptly.

Where is Fridley, Minnesota, and what does its housing stock look like?

Fridley is a first-ring suburb in the southern tip of Anoka County, directly north of Minneapolis, with 30,829 residents in the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. It became a village in 1949 and a city in 1957, and most of its growth came between 1950 and 1970. That timing means a large share of Fridley's housing dates from the postwar decades.

The city is long from north to south and narrow from east to west, following the Mississippi River and the highways beside it. It borders Minneapolis, Columbia Heights, New Brighton, Mounds View, Spring Lake Park, Blaine, Coon Rapids, Brooklyn Park and Brooklyn Center. Rice Creek crosses the middle of town, and East Moore, West Moore and Locke lakes sit inside the city limits. Land area is about 10.2 square miles.

The area was first called Manomin, after the Ojibwe word for wild rice. John Banfill became the first settler in 1847, and the Legislature renamed the township for Abram Fridley in 1879. East River Road still follows the old Red River oxcart trail.

What do the Census numbers show about Fridley homeowners and renters?

Fridley has a larger share of renters and lower home values than the other three cities in this part of the metro that the Census compares. The Census Bureau lists 63.0 percent of units as owner-occupied and a median value of $302,900 for 2020-2024. That leaves roughly 37 percent of households renting, so investors and landlords are a regular part of the buyer pool.

Which Fridley city code rules should a seller check before listing?

Fridley enforces exterior and yard standards that a buyer's inspector or the city may flag, so walk the property first. The city's code enforcement page lists the items it sees most often.

  • Grass and weeds taller than an average of ten inches draw a ten-day notice, and the city mows and bills the owner if it is not cut.
  • Driveways must be paved or hard-surfaced, and gravel driveways are not allowed.
  • Garbage, recycling and compost containers belong behind the front setback and may sit at the curb only from 5:00 PM the day before collection to 9:00 PM on collection day.
  • Vehicles parked outside need current tabs and must be street operable, and cars cannot park on grass.
  • Fences top out at four feet in the front yard and seven feet in side and rear yards.

When a violation is not fixed, the city can have a contractor correct it and add the cost to the property's taxes, or issue a citation with court fees of at least $300. An owner can appeal in writing to the City Clerk within 14 business days. Clearing open notices before a buyer's walk-through avoids last-minute credits.

Does a Fridley rental house need a city license when it sells?

Fridley licenses rental property, so a buyer who plans to keep the house as a rental should expect to apply for a license. The city uses two license subtypes: single family covers one to three units, and multi-family covers four or more. Applications go through the CitizenServe portal.

The owner must list a physical address, not a PO box. If the owner lives more than 50 miles from the property, a local contact is required. New owners can upload their purchase documents with the application because the owner shown in the portal comes from Anoka County records, which update every one to two months. Questions go to Fridley rental licensing at 763-572-3616.

If you are selling a rental and want the transaction to move smoothly, bring a copy of the current license certificate and any inspection results to the table.

How do I stop and transfer the Fridley water account at closing?

Tell the city's Utility Billing Division before your closing date, using the Moving In/Out form or by phoning 763-572-3529. Staff need a meter reading on the day of closing to prepare the seller's final bill, and the account switches to the new owner as of that date.

  • Residential water has a fixed charge of $26.01 per quarter plus tiered volume rates in the city's 2026 schedule.
  • Sewer is billed on winter-quarter water use, and recycling is $11.60 per quarter for homes.
  • Weekly garbage service comes from a private hauler licensed by the city, separate from the city bill.

Unpaid utility charges can become a lien and be sent to Anoka County to be collected with next year's property taxes. Notices go out on or before October 1 for balances billed through July 31. A 10 percent late fee can apply to past-due accounts.

What schools, roads and employers draw buyers to Fridley?

Fridley Public Schools, Independent School District 14, run Fridley High School, Fridley Middle School, Hayes Elementary and Stevenson Elementary. Parts of the city fall in other districts: a small northern area is in Anoka-Hennepin District 11, an eastern area is in Columbia Heights District 13, and much of the north-northeast belongs to Spring Lake Park District 16. Check the district for the exact address when you write the listing.

Interstate 694 and Minnesota Highways 47 and 65 are the main roads, and the Northstar commuter rail line stops at the Fridley station. The Medtronic operational headquarters, Unity Medical Center, a Target distribution center and the BNSF Northtown rail yard are among the larger employers and landmarks. Only about 21 percent of residents worked in the city in 2000, and the Census puts the average commute today at 22.6 minutes.

What does recording a Fridley deed cost in Anoka County?

Anoka County records Fridley deeds, and its fee schedule effective July 1, 2025 lists a $46 recording fee for abstract property, a $5 conservation fee and a $54 well certificate. State deed tax is 0.0033 of the net consideration over $3,000. On a sale at Fridley's $302,900 median value, that is about $1,000.

Property tax payments go to Anoka County Property Records and Taxation at 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, or online through PayAnokaCounty. The online system adds a 2.6 percent fee for cards and a $3.50 fee for e-checks, while checks and in-person payments at the Government Center carry no fee. State law splits the year's tax into two halves due before May 16 and October 16 (Minnesota Statutes 279.01), so the second half for 2026 has already come due.

Can I sell a Fridley house that has code violations?

Often, yes, but check the notice first. The city can add abatement costs to the property's taxes, and buyers often ask for credits. A cash buyer takes the property as-is, while a retail buyer may ask you to fix flagged items first.

Who do I call to close my Fridley water account?

Call the Fridley Utility Billing Division at 763-572-3529 before closing. The city needs a meter reading on the closing date, and the closing date ends the seller's account and starts the buyer's.

How much is deed tax on a Fridley home sale?

It is 0.0033 of the net sale price once consideration exceeds $3,000. At $302,900, that is roughly $1,000. Anoka County collects it with a $5 conservation fee when the deed is recorded.

Does the buyer of my Fridley rental need a rental license?

The city licenses rentals of one to three units and of four or more units, and a new owner applies through CitizenServe. The owner of record comes from Anoka County, so the application lets new owners upload purchase papers while that record catches up.

Do I have to disclose problems with my Fridley house?

Yes. Before you sign a purchase agreement, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know that could significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment of the property. The disclosure must be made in good faith.

What are your options for selling a house fast in Shoreview?

Shoreview sellers can go through an agent, find a buyer privately, or accept a cash offer for the house in its present condition. The right pick depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close.

Shoreview is a mature suburb. The city had 25,043 residents in 2010 and 26,921 at the 2020 count, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 26,906 shows almost no change since. Growth has been flat for years, so most sales are of existing houses.

  • List with an agent when the house is clean, updated and you can accept showings for several weeks.
  • Sell directly when you already have a buyer in mind and can handle the purchase agreement and disclosures.
  • Choose cash when the house needs work, is a rental, sits in an estate, or you need a firm closing date.

What is Shoreview like for a seller?

Shoreview is a second-ring suburb north of Saint Paul in Ramsey County, incorporated as a city on April 23, 1957. It has seven lakes, led by Turtle Lake, Snail Lake, Lake Owasso and Island Lake, and Rice Creek crosses the northwest corner. Interstate 35W, Interstate 694 and County Highway 96 are its main routes (Wikipedia).

The city covers 10.77 square miles of land, about 2,500 people per square mile. Two school districts serve it, Mounds View (District 621) and Roseville (District 623), so a buyer's school assignment depends on which side of the district line a house sits.

Shoreview has nine city parks and three county parks, and the Shamrock Park site was a rest stop for travelers as early as the late 1840s. The city's 2025 year in review shows what is being built around you. Nearly 2,000 permits were issued through September 30, with more than $36.5 million in construction value, including the Seven Lakes office buildings and several new apartment projects such as the Aloma Apartments, the third building beside Emrik and Loden SV. The city also approved the subdivision of a former apple orchard into 13 single-family homes, and it is rewriting its development code, with changes on grading and erosion control and on ground-mounted solar arrays.

Shoreview's permit and rental rules decide how much cleanup a sale needs. Any open or missing permit is easier to settle before a buyer's inspection than after.

  • Permits: contractors apply online for residential roofing, siding, windows, doors, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work. Homeowners email applications to permits@shoreviewmn.gov or bring them to City Hall.
  • Plan review: permits that need plan review typically take up to 10 working days.
  • Smaller jobs: fences, driveways, patios and sheds of 200 square feet or less go through Community Development at 651-490-4680.
  • Safety items: the city publishes handouts for decks, egress windows, finished basements, smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms.

If a sale involves a lake lot or a sloped yard, ask Community Development whether the erosion and sediment control handout applies to your project, since the city is updating its grading standards. Overnight street parking is not allowed from 2 to 5 a.m. A permit covers up to seven days and five vehicles, which helps during a move-out, though dumpsters and storage pods may not sit on the street.

Does Shoreview license rental houses, and what happens when one is sold?

Yes. Every rental property in Shoreview needs a rental license, and the city issues one only when the unit meets city regulations and municipal utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full. The city lists more than 600 rental locations.

There are three license types: a general dwelling license for a single-family home with an inspection every other year, a short-term rental license for stays of 30 days or less with an annual inspection and extra parking rules, and a multiple dwelling license for four or more units. Licenses expire December 31 and renew each year. The 2025 year in review notes the city began licensing short-term rentals and inspected over 300 rental homes that year (City of Shoreview).

If you sell a rented house, the city provides a form to void the license once the property is sold. Settle that, and any unpaid utility bill, at the closing table so the next owner starts clean.

How do Ramsey County notices and records affect a Shoreview sale?

Ramsey County sends two mailings each year. The first arrives in mid-March and holds the tax statement, which shows both half-year amounts, plus a notice of valuation and classification that sets next year's taxes. The second comes in November and lists proposed taxes and the dates of levy and budget meetings.

The county's Property Tax Services office is at 90 Plato Boulevard West in Saint Paul, reachable at 651-266-2222. Deeds and mortgages are recorded with the Ramsey County Recorder and Registrar of Titles at 651-266-2050. The office does not help complete legal forms, and a recorded document is permanent, so have the deed reviewed before it goes in.

  • Ask Property Tax Services for the amount due on both halves of the current year.
  • Ask the Recorder which document types the sale needs, since fees and requirements differ by document.
  • For an estate sale, confirm who has authority to sign before scheduling the closing.
  • Watch the November mailing: it previews next year's taxes and the budget meetings where residents can comment, which a buyer may ask about.

A cash sale can close in a few weeks when the title is clear, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. A lien, an unpaid utility bill or an unsettled estate can lengthen that. In a suburb where about four in five homes are owner-occupied, a seller who is renting out the house should also settle the tenant's move-out date first.

Does Shoreview require a rental license for a single-family house?

Yes. A single-family rental needs a general dwelling rental license, which includes an inspection every other year, and the license renews each December 31. The city issues it only when utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full.

What happens to a Shoreview rental license when I sell?

You can void the license with the city's form once the property has sold. Doing it promptly stops renewal notices and shows the city the unit changed hands. The city's rental license page lists the fee schedule on page 2 of its PDF if you need to check what a license cost.

When does Ramsey County mail property tax notices?

The tax statement and value notice go out in mid-March, and the proposed tax notice arrives in November. The statement shows the first and second half amounts for the year.

Is a permit needed to fix up a Shoreview house before listing?

Often yes. Roofing, siding, windows, doors, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work all need permits, and fences, driveways and small sheds go through zoning. Call building inspections at 651-490-4683 to confirm before starting.

Permits are usually needed for additions, decks, garages, fences, pools, water heaters, re-roofing and electrical, plumbing and heating work.

Two routine ordinances also generate liens against sellers who ignore them.

  • Grass and weeds. City Code 10.13 sets an 8 inch height limit. After a notice from the weed inspector you have seven days to comply, then the city cuts it and certifies the cost to the Mower County Auditor as a special assessment collected like real estate taxes.
  • Sidewalk snow. Chapter 7.04 requires owners to clear public sidewalks within 12 hours after snow stops, and the city may clear them after 24 hours and bill the owner.

Deal with both before closing, since an unpaid assessment is collected the way real estate taxes are. Austin also does not allow chickens, which matters if you kept hens and a buyer asks about the coop.

Do Austin rental registration rules apply when you sell?

They apply if the house is a rental, and they can affect the buyer. Austin requires residential rental property to be registered under City Ordinance 4.29, and the city's rental program FAQ says a Change of Ownership form must be filed when a rental is sold. Ask the city whether the same tenants will stay with the new owner, because that decides which form is used.

If you live elsewhere for part of the year, the program also asks you to name a local rental manager who handles emergencies and inspections. Anyone planning to keep the tenants will want to see the rental registration and any inspection results, so pull those documents together before a deal is signed.

How do Mower County property taxes work at closing?

Mower County bills property tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and second-half agricultural tax is due November 15. The Auditor-Treasurer's office is in the Government Center at 201 First Street NE, Suite 7, in Austin, and the phone is 507-437-9535.

  • The county does not mail second-half statements, so a buyer should ask for the amount.
  • Mail payments are judged by postmark, and a private postage meter mark does not count.
  • The county will not accept post-dated checks.
  • A missing statement does not excuse a late payment.

On the deed side, Minnesota Statute 287.21 sets the state deed tax at .0033 of the net consideration when the price is above $3,000, and the Hennepin County recorder's checklist adds that an eCRV is required for sales over $3,000 and that a deed cannot pass title while taxes are delinquent. A well statement or well disclosure certificate also has to accompany a transfer deed. Ask the Mower County recorder for the local filing steps and fees.

What must you tell a buyer in writing?

Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know before the purchase agreement is signed. It covers facts that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment of the property, made in good faith and to the best of your knowledge. A separate radon statute, section 144.496, adds a written radon disclosure and a copy of the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

For an Austin house, the facts buyers care about most are basement water, past flooding, roof and furnace age, and any work done without a permit. Writing these down early keeps negotiations short, and it matters even more in a quick sale where the buyer is not hiring an inspector.

More questions about Austin, MN

Do I need an inspection from the city before selling in Austin?

Ask the building department at City Hall, 500 4th Avenue NE, whether any sale-time step applies to your address, and gather your permits and any rental registration so a buyer can see them.

What happens if I have unpermitted work on my Austin house?

A buyer may be able to require you to remove it, leave it unoccupied or pay for repairs. The city's FAQ says exactly that about modifications made without a permit, so ask the building office whether the work can be permitted after the fact before you list.

What are the due dates for Mower County tax?

May 15 and October 15, with second-half agricultural tax due November 15. The county does not mail second-half statements, so request the figure from the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-437-9535 if you need it for closing.

Can a high weed or grass notice block my sale?

It will not block the sale by itself, but unpaid mowing costs become a special assessment on the parcel. Austin allows 8 inches of grass and gives seven days after notice, so cut it early and ask the clerk for any pending charges.

Is Austin a good place to sell to a landlord or investor?

Often yes. Median rent is $953 and 71.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so investors look at the town. Registered rentals must follow Austin's rental ordinance, and a sold rental needs a Change of Ownership form filed with the city.
