What is it like to sell a house in Winona?

Selling in Winona means selling into a small river city with a large student population and a lot of rental property. Houses here are far less expensive than in the Twin Cities suburbs, and the local rules that matter most are about rentals, permits and short-term stays.

Winona sits on the Mississippi River in the Driftless Area, about 44 miles from Rochester and 30 miles from La Crosse. A seller can list with an agent, sell privately or take a direct cash offer. Which one makes sense usually depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close.

What do the Census numbers say about Winona housing?

The Census Bureau counted 26,530 residents on July 1, 2025, up 2.1% from the April 2020 base of 25,997. The city had lost people between 2010 and 2020, so the recent gain is a reversal.

  • 10,786 households averaging 2.13 people
  • 58.0% of homes owner-occupied (2020 to 2024)
  • Median owner-occupied value: $201,800
  • Median gross rent: $882
  • Median household income: $56,337, with 23.1% of residents below the poverty line
  • 18.9% of residents 65 or older, and 12.5% under 18

The 2020 census found a median age of 31.6 and 39.2% of households with one person living alone. Many Winona sellers are older owners downsizing or heirs handling a parent's house, and many buyers are first-time buyers or investors.

How did Winona grow, and why does it matter for older houses?

Settlers laid out the town in 1852 and 1853 on land the Dakota had known as the village of Keoxa. Population jumped from 815 in December 1855 to 3,000 a year later. Steamboats, lumber, wheat milling and railroads built the economy, and more than 1,300 steamboats stopped in 1856.

German immigrants arrived in 1856, and between 1859 and 1900 about 5,000 Poles and Kashubians settled in the city, roughly a quarter of the population. That history left two historic districts on the National Register of Historic Places that combine into one local historic district under the city's Heritage Preservation Commission. If your house is in that district, ask the city's planning office what review applies before you promise a buyer changes to the exterior.

What local conditions affect a Winona house?

The land is hilly bluff country with a river on one side. The city covers 24.32 square miles, of which 19.03 are land and 5.29 are water, and Lock and Dam 5A crosses the river here. Latsch Island, connected by bridges and part of the city since 1998, holds a community of houseboat residents.

The weather station at Winona records the warmest normal temperature of any in Minnesota, a yearly average of 48.9 degrees Fahrenheit. The January mean is 17.6 and the July mean is 75.8, so houses face hot humid summers and cold snowy winters. Buyers commonly ask about basements, furnaces and roofs, and about whether a property near the river sits in a mapped floodplain. Ask the city's inspections office or your insurer to confirm the status of your address.

How do Winona's rental license rules affect a seller?

Any rental unit in the city must hold a license before tenants move in, and Chapter 33A of the housing code requires an inspection every five years. If you rent out the house you are selling, the inspection and license status will come up in the buyer's due diligence.

The licensing steps on the city page are short:

  1. Planning and Zoning confirms that the property may be a rental.
  2. The owner submits a rental license application.
  3. The Building Inspections Department inspects the unit.
  4. The fee is paid, due upfront for a new rental.
  5. The property must meet the housing code before the license is issued.

The city also provides a Rental License Transfer of Ownership application, which a buyer of a rental house will need. Call Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 to ask whether your property qualifies as a rental, and the inspections office at 507-457-8231 to schedule.

How much does a Winona rental inspection cost?

The city charges an inspection fee once every five years for certification. The schedule below took effect January 1, 2026, under City Code Chapter 51.

Winona rental housing inspection fees effective January 1, 2026, from the City of Winona Inspections Department
Property typeCalculationTotal
Single-family dwelling$100 per unit plus $100 per building$200
Duplex$200 for two units plus $100 per building$300
Owner-occupied duplex$100 for one unit plus $100 per building$200
Sleeping room$45 per room plus $100 per building$145 for one room

The owner's own unit in an owner-occupied duplex is not certified, which is why it is charged for one unit only.

Can a buyer use a Winona house as a short-term rental?

Only with a license and a public hearing. The city calls short-term rentals Tourist Homes and defines them as buildings that provide sleeping accommodations to transient guests for up to 29 consecutive days. There are two classes, owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied, each with its own regulations.

  • Every short-term rental must be inspected and licensed
  • Residential zoning districts require a Planning Commission public hearing before licensing
  • A 4% hotel and motel tax on monthly rent has applied since July 1, 2018

If your house has been used for Airbnb-style stays, gather the license paperwork for the buyer. If it has not, assume a new owner cannot start without the hearing.

What repairs and permits come up before closing in Winona?

A building permit is required for additions, alterations, new construction, remodeling and most replacements. Work that does not need one includes painting, cabinets, countertops, floor coverings, tiling, storage sheds under 200 square feet, retaining walls up to 4 feet and decks not over 30 inches above grade, unless attached to a permanent structure.

Fences usually need no permit, but ask Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 first. Fences may reach 6 feet in the rear and 4 feet on the street side, and anything over 7 feet needs a variance and a permit. The city does not issue electrical permits, so electrical questions go to the state electrical inspector. An unpermitted deck or finished basement is something a buyer's inspector will notice, so close out any open permits before you list.

What taxes and paperwork apply when a Winona house sells?

The county auditor receives a certificate of real estate value for any sale above $3,000, and Minnesota Statutes 272.115 bars homestead status for the buyer if it is missing. The assessor drops the homestead classification after a sale until the new owner applies and qualifies.

Property sits in Winona County, so the deed is recorded with the county recorder there. Ask the county for current recording fees and the deed tax calculation, and have your title company confirm who files the certificate. Minnesota also lets a seller pass the required disclosure to the buyer's agent instead of the buyer directly.

Who works and studies in Winona, and who buys homes there?

The city's 2022 financial report lists Fastenal as the largest employer at 1,618 people, followed by Winona State University at 1,050, Winona Health at 975 and Winona Area Public Schools at 684. Saint Mary's University of Minnesota, WinCraft, RTP Company and Winona County government also employ hundreds.

Winona State, Saint Mary's and Minnesota State College Southeast bring students and staff who rent, which explains the large rental license program. Highways 14, 61 and 43 lead into the city, Amtrak's Empire Builder and Borealis stop at the old Milwaukee Road depot, and Winona Transit Service runs buses six days a week. Mean travel time to work is 13.8 minutes.

More questions about Winona, MN

Does Winona require an inspection before I sell my house?

Winona's inspection program covers rental units, which need a license renewed through an inspection every five years. For a house you live in, ask the inspections office at 507-457-8231 whether anything applies to your address.

How much is a rental inspection in Winona?

A single-family rental costs $200 total, made of $100 per unit and $100 per building, under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. A duplex is $300.

Can I sell a rental house to a new owner in Winona?

Yes. The buyer files a Rental License Transfer of Ownership application, and the property must still meet the housing code. Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 can confirm that the property is eligible.

Are Airbnb stays allowed in Winona?

They are allowed with a license. The city treats them as Tourist Homes for stays up to 29 days, requires an inspection and a hearing in residential districts, and charges a 4% hotel and motel tax.

What is the typical home value in Winona?

The Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied value at $201,800 for 2020 to 2024. Your own number depends on condition and location, so get a written offer or a local agent's estimate before you decide.

How would you describe Farmington, Minnesota, to someone selling a home there?

Farmington sits in southern Dakota County on the metro's outer rim, and nearly nine in ten homes are owner-occupied. Mid-2025 Census estimates count 25,425 people, up 7.4 percent from the April 2020 base. Roughly 14.6 square miles of land make up the city, which touches Lakeville on its west side, Empire Township on the east, and Castle Rock and Eureka townships to the south.

Locals split town along County Highway 50. The older downtown lies south of that road, where only a couple of large projects have gone in over two decades. North of it, subdivisions are newer, and a third growth area spreads east into Empire Township. A trail along the Vermillion River ties downtown, uptown and the Empire-side neighborhoods together, a feature worth mentioning in a listing or an offer conversation.

The city got its charter in 1872, making it the second-oldest community in Dakota County after Hastings. A fire on November 22, 1879 destroyed several houses, stores, a hotel and a grain elevator downtown. Growth came late: the 2000 count was 12,365, and by 2010 it had reached 21,086.

What do Farmington's housing numbers say about my sale?

The median owner-occupied home in Farmington is valued at $366,200 in five-year survey data covering 2020 through 2024, and 86.5 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners. A seller here is usually competing with other single-family houses, with few apartments in the mix.

At 27.7 minutes, the average commute is the longest of the four cities in the Census comparison, so many households drive a good distance to their jobs.

Another number worth knowing: 29.1 percent of Farmington residents are under 18, the highest share among the four cities in that comparison, against 24.2 percent in Fridley and 20.8 percent in Inver Grove Heights. Families with children are a large part of the local population, which is worth keeping in mind when you describe the house. Owners without a mortgage report median monthly costs of $781, which is a useful benchmark when a buyer asks what it costs to carry the house.

How do I close out the Farmington city water account when I sell?

Call Farmington Utility Billing at 651-280-6883 before closing to book a final meter reading. The city does not shut water off when someone moves out, so the account keeps running until you close it.

  • Utility bills come quarterly, and the city bills water, sewer, storm water and street lights.
  • Trash and recycling are billed separately by Dick's Sanitation, which handles cancellations at 952-469-2239.
  • Any unpaid final utility bill is certified to the property as a special assessment, so a buyer's title company may hold money back at closing if the account is open.

Landlords selling a rental should know that Farmington keeps rental utility accounts in the owner's name, so the owner has to close the account, not the tenant. A late fee of 10 percent applies to rental accounts that fall behind. Ask Utility Billing for the exact balance on your closing date rather than estimating it from the last bill.

Which schools, roads and employers matter to Farmington buyers?

Farmington Area Public Schools, Independent School District 192, enrolls about 6,900 students. Its attendance area takes in Farmington, eastern Lakeville, and Castle Rock, Empire and Eureka townships. A Lakeville address can therefore sit in a different district, so confirm the district for the exact street before you write a listing.

Main routes are Minnesota Highway 3, Minnesota Highway 50, and Dakota County Roads 31 and 50. A federal air traffic control center for the upper Midwest operates here, and a Kemps packing plant is another long-standing employer. The Dakota County Fairgrounds, about 360 acres with gates on 220th Street and Highway 3, report the highest county fair attendance in the state.

  • Price point: the $366,200 median value compares with $452,500 in neighboring Lakeville.
  • Commute: the 27.7 minute average drive to work is long for the metro.

What are the quickest ways to sell a Farmington house?

Three routes exist: an agent listing, a sale handled on your own, or an as-is purchase by a cash buyer. Each one trades speed against price and effort.

  • Agent listing: strongest when the house shows well and you can ride out inspections and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Do it yourself: skips the commission, though marketing, forms and haggling fall to you.
  • Cash buyer: fits inherited houses, deferred repairs, tenant-occupied rentals and owners behind on payments, since the buyer accepts the house in its present state and the closing date can follow your schedule.

Whatever you choose, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 obliges you to hand the buyer a written disclosure of known material facts before a purchase agreement is signed. Condition questions differ by area: subdivisions north of County Highway 50 are mostly under twenty years old, while downtown houses are older.

What happens at the Dakota County recorder when a Farmington deed is filed?

The county's records office in Hastings handles every Farmington deed. Walk-in filing is by appointment at the Administration Center, and mailed packets go to 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings with a return envelope. Most parcels countywide are abstract property, so your title company will search the record before closing.

Minnesota's deed tax equals the net sale price times 0.0033. At Farmington's $366,200 median, expect about $1,208. A deed also has to carry a well disclosure certificate, or a line stating the seller knows of no wells (Minnesota Statutes 103I.235). Before a deed is accepted, the county auditor looks for delinquent taxes (Minnesota Statutes 272.12). Recording charges are fixed by state law and posted on the county's fee page, so your title company can quote the total.

When are Farmington property taxes due, and who pays at closing?

Dakota County bills in two installments, May 15 and October 15 in 2026, and the autumn one is now behind us. A missed half costs 2 percent on a homestead and 4 percent otherwise, with monthly additions through December (Minnesota Statutes 279.01).

Settlement statements normally split the current year's bill between buyer and seller by closing date. Check the county's parcel search for open balances ahead of listing. The next homestead application deadline is December 31.

If you owe back taxes, ask Dakota County Property Taxation and Records for the payoff amount. Keep your latest tax statement handy so you can confirm the parcel number and the amounts already paid.

More questions about Farmington, MN

How quickly can I close on a Farmington house?

A cash purchase can close on a date you choose, frequently within a few weeks, since no lender appraisal is involved. Listing with an agent generally runs longer. For either path, book the water meter reading with Farmington Utility Billing in advance.

Are repairs required before I sell in Farmington?

The disclosure statute asks for a written statement of material facts you know before a purchase agreement is signed, and it does not list required repairs. Cash buyers take the house as it stands. Retail buyers often negotiate fixes after an inspection.

What becomes of an unpaid Farmington utility bill after a sale?

It stays attached to the property. The city certifies unpaid water, sewer, storm drainage and street light charges as a special assessment, so buyers' title companies usually want the last bill settled. A final read keeps the number accurate.

Who files the deed for a Farmington sale?

Dakota County's records office in Hastings, normally through your title company. The state sets the fees, the deed tax is 0.0033 of the net price, and the deed needs either a well certificate or a no-wells statement.

Can I sell Farmington rental property while tenants live there?

Yes. Go over the lease terms with the buyer and your title company. Farmington keeps rental utility accounts in the owner's name, so plan to close that account on the sale date.
